title: Home's agent panel
subtitle: Decision walkthrough · 10 Nov 2026 · narrated by Duo's house voice
posterLine: What the column costs, five ways out, then five decisions. Tap play and listen; it stops when it needs you.
footer: Built with the decision-walkthrough skill from docs/research/home-agent-panel-walkthrough/spec.json. Answers are saved in this page and sent to director-duo-v2.

said.ENH-322: E N H three twenty two

lines.text: This is the study of Home's agent panel, and it ends in five decisions.
The Claude session in this left column at All projects is Home's agent.
On November third you said you weren't sure most people would use it, and that we were building strange workarounds for it.
Today, after Oliver's black terminal, you asked for options: gate it in Settings, or make starting it a deliberate act.
Everything wrong with it comes from three facts.
It's narrow. Questions are drawn at thirty-eight to forty-three columns, and chat sends two to four of seventeen question shapes to the terminal.
It lives in two places: one terminal, two slots in one window. That's the black terminal Oliver saw, and Show Here in every other window.
And it runs unseen. Since DL-315 the column starts closed, but Duo still starts Home's Claude at every launch. I checked: a fresh Duo lists a session nobody started.
I looked at five ways out.
A, a Settings switch, and B, starting it only when asked, are your two ideas.
C moves Home's agent to Home's own page. D keeps the column and makes it fit. E is a Sessions view, for later.
I recommend C. It's your second idea carried through, because the deliberate action already exists.

chapters.title: What happens to the column
chapters.ask: What happens to Home's agent panel at All projects?
chapters.why: The column is narrow, lives in two places, and runs unseen.

look.label: Canvas · boards C1 and C2 (recommended), A, B, D2

lines.text: So, what happens to the column?

options.label: C: Home's agent on Home's page only
options.desc: No column at All projects; New session in ★ home starts one; Home's questions get full cards. About two sessions, mostly removal.

lines.text: I recommend C. All projects is the list and Needs you, and Home's agent runs on Home's page at a full console's width. About two sessions, mostly removing code.

options.label: A: a Settings switch, off by default
options.desc: Fixes it for people who leave it off; keeps every workaround for those who turn it on.

lines.text: A adds a Settings switch, off by default. It fixes things for people who leave it off, and keeps every workaround for those who don't.

options.label: B: a start card; nothing runs until asked
options.desc: Fixes the unseen session; once started it's today's column.

lines.text: B shows a start card the first time the column opens, and runs nothing until then. Once started, it's today's column.

options.label: D: keep the column, make questions fit
options.desc: A 60-column floor (Q-488 a) or a 480-wide column. The two places and the launch start stay.

lines.text: D keeps the column and makes questions fit, with a sixty column floor or a wider column.

chapters.title: Starting Home at launch
chapters.ask: Should Duo still start a Home session at launch?
chapters.why: DL-54 starts one whenever Home has none, even with the column closed.

lines.text: Whichever you pick, should Duo still start a Home session at launch?

options.label: No: start it on first use
options.desc: Home's page shows Start Claude in Home; the list's New session row starts one. Reverses DL-54.

lines.text: I recommend no. Duo waits until it's first used. Home's page shows Start Claude in Home, and the list's New session row starts one.

options.label: Yes: keep DL-54
options.desc: Home's agent is always ready, out of sight.

lines.text: Or keep DL-54, and Home's agent is always ready, out of sight.

chapters.title: Telling people who use it
chapters.ask: How do people who use the column today learn where Home's agent went?
chapters.why: Only matters if the column goes (C).

lines.text: If the column goes, how do people who use it find Home's agent?

options.label: A release note only
options.desc: Their sessions don't move; ★ home and ⇧⌘H reach them.

lines.text: I recommend a release note only. DL-315 already closed the column for nearly everyone, and their sessions don't move.

options.label: A one-time line at All projects
options.desc: For installs whose column was open. A new surface to draw.

lines.text: Or a one-time line at All projects for anyone whose column was open. That's a new thing to draw.

chapters.title: The sidebar button at All projects
chapters.ask: With no column, what do the sidebar button and ⌃⌘S do at All projects?
chapters.why: Only matters if the column goes (C).

lines.text: With no column, what does the sidebar button do at All projects?

options.label: Hidden at All projects
options.desc: The button and ⌃⌘S go there; duo2 view sidebar says All projects has no sidebar.

lines.text: I recommend hiding it there, with ⌃⌘S. duo2 says there's no sidebar.

options.label: Keep it for a projects sidebar later

lines.text: Or keep it for a sidebar of projects later, which needs its own design.

chapters.title: Questions in a narrow pane
chapters.ask: How should chat stop falling back on questions in a narrow pane?
chapters.why: Narrow consoles remain even without the column: narrow windows, split view.

lines.text: Last, Q-488. I ran the question suite again: four of seventeen fall back at thirty-eight columns, two at forty-three, and none at sixty.

options.label: (a) Hold the hidden terminal at 60 columns or more
options.desc: While chat shows, whatever the pane's width; and take F-641's mic margin off. Small.

lines.text: I recommend holding the hidden terminal at sixty columns or more while chat shows, and fixing F-641's slip.

options.label: (b) Teach the matcher the narrow layouts
options.desc: Each narrow layout proved in the live suite.

lines.text: Or teach the reader each narrow layout, one by one.
Or leave it, and the terminal answers them.
That's all five.
Each answer went to the director as you saved it, and Copy decisions puts them all on the clipboard.
